# onetsolutions_dns_record (Resource)

Manages a record in a DNS zone.

Equivalent spellings (`@` or the zone name for the apex, relative or fully qualified names, quoted
or unquoted TXT values, with or without a trailing dot) are treated as equal and never show as a
diff.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onetsolutions_dns_zone" "example" {
  zone_name = "example.com"
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_record" "apex" {
  zone_id = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.id
  type    = "A"
  name    = "@"
  content = "203.0.113.10"
  ttl     = 300
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_id = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.id
  type    = "CNAME"
  name    = "www"
  content = "example.com"
  proxied = true
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_record" "mail" {
  zone_id  = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.id
  type     = "MX"
  name     = "@"
  content  = "mail.example.net"
  priority = 10
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_record" "spf" {
  zone_id = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.id
  type    = "TXT"
  name    = "@"
  content = "v=spf1 mx -all"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The value of the record: an IPv4 address for `A`, an IPv6 address for `AAAA`, a host name for `CNAME`, `MX`, `NS` and `PTR`, the text for `TXT` (quoted or not), `weight port target` for `SRV`, `flags tag "value"` for `CAA`.
- `name` (String) The name of the record: `@` (or the zone name) for the apex, a name relative to the zone such as `www`, or a fully qualified name inside the zone.
- `type` (String) The record type, one of `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT`, `NS`, `SRV`, `CAA`, `PTR`. Changing it recreates the record.
- `zone_id` (String) The UUID of the zone (see `onetsolutions_dns_zone`). Changing it recreates the record.

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `priority` (Number) The priority, between 0 and 65535; required for `MX` and `SRV` records.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `proxied` (Boolean) Route the traffic through the edge network (`A`, `AAAA` and `CNAME` only). Defaults to `false`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `ttl` (Number) The time to live, in seconds: `1` (automatic) or between 60 and 86400. When unset, defaults to 3600, or to automatic on a proxied record, which only accepts `1`.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) When the record was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) The UUID of the record.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the deletion, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `5m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `5m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_dns_record.www
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<zone_id>/<record_id>, or <zone_id>/<record_id> when the provider
# sets organization_id and project_id. An import writes the canonical spelling: "@" for the apex,
# names relative to the zone, TXT values unquoted.
terraform import onetsolutions_dns_record.www 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d
```
